title: Measure elapsed time across rollover
description: Implement int deadline_reached(uint32_t now, uint32_t start, uint32_t interval).
prompt:
Implement int deadline_reached(uint32_t now, uint32_t start, uint32_t interval).
Return 1 when at least interval ticks have elapsed since start, otherwise 0. now and start are readings of one wrapping 32-bit counter. The actual elapsed duration is less than 2^32 ticks.
constraints: The timer wraps from UINT32_MAX to zero.
Do not compare now against start + interval.

tests.name: Before deadline
At deadline
Rollover
Zero interval
Before wrapped deadline

reference_solution.solution.c:
#include <stdint.h>
int deadline_reached(uint32_t now, uint32_t start, uint32_t interval) { return (uint32_t)(now - start) >= interval; }

rubric: Respect the stated contract and bounds.
Explain integer widths, ownership, and relevant edge cases.
Separate host-test evidence from hardware guarantees.
follow_ups: What if this function is not called for an entire timer period?
How would you convert milliseconds to ticks without overflowing?
hints: Write down the boundary cases before choosing an implementation.
Use explicit integer widths and keep intermediate values in range.
